q: Do regenerative burners cut furnace fuel and emissions?
title: Regenerative burners: fuel saving
short: Yes, often substantially. Regenerative burners work in pairs: one fires while the other stores heat from the exhaust in a ceramic bed, then they swap, so combustion air arrives very hot. Less fuel heats the same steel. Prove the saving with fuel per tonne before and after.
audience: Reheating furnace, forging and aluminium melting operators

sections.h: How it differs from a recuperator
ul: A recuperator passes exhaust heat through a metal heat exchanger, limited by the metal temperature.
A regenerative pair stores heat in ceramic media, so the air can be preheated much hotter.
Higher flame temperatures can raise NOx; ask about low-NOx designs.
Dusty or corrosive exhaust can foul the ceramic bed.
Controls must handle the switching cycle.

p: Compare fuel per tonne heated over a few months before and after, at similar throughput. Multiply the fuel saved by its factor, for example 2.05 kg CO2 per scm of natural gas.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
